name: Dwarika's Hotel
summary: A heritage hotel at Battisputali, near Pashupatinath, built around brick courtyards and fitted with carved Newar windows, doors and struts rescued from old valley buildings. It is the most complete showcase of Newar woodwork you can sleep in, and a calm retreat from the city's traffic.
body: Dwarika's grew out of one man's rescue work. From the 1950s onwards, Dwarika Das Shrestha began collecting carved windows, pillars and doors from old Newar houses that were being torn down across the valley, and set his craftsmen to restore them. The hotel was built to give that woodwork a home, so the courtyards, corridors and rooms are set with genuine old carvings alongside new pieces made by local artisans.

Rooms are spread across low brick buildings round courtyards and gardens, with terracotta, handloom fabrics and carved details. The hotel's Krishnarpan restaurant serves a long, multi-course Nepali meal, and other restaurants on site serve international food. The location, a few minutes from Pashupatinath and about 15 minutes from Boudha and the airport, suits travellers who want to be near the eastern sights rather than in Thamel.
why: Genuine Newar carvings rescued from valley buildings, restored on site
Quiet courtyards and gardens, close to Pashupatinath and Boudha
A long Nepali tasting meal at Krishnarpan

faqs.q: Where is Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Dwarika's is at Battisputali in east Kathmandu, about 10 minutes' walk or a short drive from Pashupatinath, around 15 minutes from Boudhanath and about 15 to 20 minutes from the airport. Thamel and the Durbar Square are 25 to 40 minutes away by car, depending on traffic.

faqs.q: What is special about Dwarika's Hotel?
faqs.a: The hotel is built around carved Newar woodwork, windows, doors and pillars, many rescued from old valley buildings that were being demolished and then restored by craftsmen. Staying here is like living in a museum of Newar architecture, with modern comfort and quiet courtyards away from city noise.

faqs.q: What is the Krishnarpan meal at Dwarika's?
faqs.a: Krishnarpan is the hotel's Nepali restaurant, serving a long tasting menu of Nepali and Newar dishes in many small courses, from a short set to an extended feast. It is popular for special occasions, so book ahead. Vegetarian versions are available on request.

name: Hotel Yak & Yeti
summary: A large city hotel on Durbar Marg, built around part of a 19th-century Rana palace, with gardens, a pool and the old Chimney restaurant linked to Boris Lissanevitch, the Russian who ran Kathmandu's first hotels. Central, walkable to Thamel and the Narayanhiti Palace Museum.
body: Hotel Yak & Yeti stands just off Durbar Marg, Kathmandu's broad avenue running south from the Narayanhiti Palace. Part of the hotel occupies a wing of the Lal Durbar, a Rana-era palace, with its neoclassical halls and mirrored rooms used for events. Newer wings hold most of the guest rooms, set round gardens and a swimming pool that are a quiet escape from the traffic outside.

The hotel's history is tied to Boris Lissanevitch, the Russian dancer and restaurateur who ran Kathmandu's first hotel for foreigners in the 1950s and whose Yak & Yeti bar gave the hotel its name. The Chimney restaurant, which traces its story to Boris, still serves dinner. The location is a strong point: Thamel is 15 minutes on foot, the palace museum 5 minutes, and the Durbar Square about 25 minutes' walk.
why: Central Durbar Marg location, walkable to Thamel and the palace museum
Rana palace wing and the Chimney restaurant's early tourism history
Gardens and pool as a retreat from the city

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Yak & Yeti?
faqs.a: Hotel Yak & Yeti is just off Durbar Marg in central Kathmandu, a few minutes' walk from the Narayanhiti Palace Museum and about 15 minutes' walk from Thamel. The airport is about 20 to 30 minutes away by car. Kathmandu Durbar Square is about 25 minutes on foot.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Yak & Yeti a heritage hotel?
faqs.a: Partly. One wing occupies part of the Lal Durbar, a Rana-era palace, with ornate halls used for events and dining, while most guest rooms are in newer wings. Its Chimney restaurant recalls Boris Lissanevitch, a figure from Kathmandu's early days of tourism.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Yak & Yeti have a pool?
faqs.a: Yes, the hotel has an outdoor swimming pool set in its gardens, along with a fitness centre and spa services. Pool opening may be seasonal or limited in the coldest months, so check current status before you travel if a swim matters to you.

name: Hotel Shanker
summary: A Rana-era palace in Lazimpat converted into a hotel, with a white neoclassical facade, high-ceilinged halls and a large garden with a pool. Old-world and calm, 15 minutes' walk from Thamel and close to embassies and cafes.
body: Hotel Shanker occupies a palace built in the Rana period, when Nepal's ruling prime ministers and their families raised European-style mansions across Kathmandu. Its white facade, columns and stucco ornament face a sweeping lawn, and inside, the halls and staircases keep their high ceilings, chandeliers and period detail. Rooms are in the palace building and in wings around the garden.

The setting is the attraction: a large garden with a swimming pool, mature trees and seating, rare in a crowded city. Lazimpat is a quieter neighbourhood of embassies, offices and cafes, about 15 minutes' walk from Thamel and 25 minutes by car from the airport. It suits travellers who want a sense of old Kathmandu and calm evenings in the garden.
why: A real Rana-era palace with period halls and facade
Large garden and pool in a quiet part of the city
Walkable to Thamel, close to Lazimpat cafes

faqs.q: Is Hotel Shanker a real palace?
faqs.a: Yes. Hotel Shanker occupies a palace built during the Rana period, when Nepal's hereditary prime ministers built European-style mansions in Kathmandu. The building keeps its neoclassical facade, high-ceilinged halls and period details, with guest rooms in the main building and garden wings.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Shanker from Thamel?
faqs.a: About 15 minutes' walk or 5 minutes by taxi. Lazimpat is quieter than Thamel, with embassies, offices and cafes. The airport is about 25 to 30 minutes away by car, and Kathmandu Durbar Square about 15 to 20 minutes by taxi.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Shanker have a garden and pool?
faqs.a: Yes. The palace faces a large garden with an outdoor swimming pool, lawns and trees, one of the larger hotel gardens in central Kathmandu. Pool hours may be limited in winter, so check current status before you travel.

name: Kathmandu Guest House
summary: One of the first guesthouses in Thamel, opened in the late 1960s, and the place many say started the area's tourist quarter. Rooms range from simple to comfortable round a garden courtyard in the heart of Thamel, walkable to Asan and the Durbar Square.
body: Kathmandu Guest House opened in the late 1960s, when Thamel was still a quiet neighbourhood of houses and fields, and it became a base for overland travellers, trekkers and climbers. The rest of Thamel's hotels, restaurants and trekking shops grew up around it. The property was damaged in the 2015 earthquake and has since been repaired and reopened.

Today it offers rooms at several levels of comfort, from simple to deluxe, set round a garden courtyard with tables and trees, a calm spot in Thamel's lanes. The location is its strength: you can walk to Asan and Indra Chowk in 15 minutes and to the Durbar Square in 25, and trekking agencies and gear shops are on the doorstep.
why: A Thamel landmark from the late 1960s with a garden courtyard
Walkable to Asan, Indra Chowk and the Durbar Square
Range of room levels for different budgets

faqs.q: Is Kathmandu Guest House in Thamel?
faqs.a: Yes, it is in the heart of Thamel, Kathmandu's main tourist district. Restaurants, trekking agencies and gear shops are steps away. Asan and Indra Chowk are about 15 minutes' walk and Kathmandu Durbar Square about 25 minutes. The airport is 20 to 40 minutes by car.

faqs.q: Is Kathmandu Guest House noisy?
faqs.a: Thamel can be loud in the evenings, but the guest house sits back from the street round a garden courtyard, which helps. Rooms facing the garden or higher floors are usually quieter. Ask for a courtyard-facing room when you book if you are a light sleeper.

faqs.q: Was Kathmandu Guest House damaged in the 2015 earthquake?
faqs.a: Yes. The property was damaged in 2015 and has since been repaired, and the hotel has been operating fully since. The garden and courtyard remain at the centre of the property, as they have been since its early days.

name: Gokarna Forest Resort
summary: A resort inside the Gokarna forest, a former royal hunting reserve on the north-eastern edge of Kathmandu, with an 18-hole golf course, spa and indoor pool. Deer and monkeys roam the grounds, and Boudhanath and Pashupatinath are about 15 to 20 minutes away by car.
body: Gokarna forest is one of the largest patches of old woodland left within the Kathmandu Valley, once the private hunting reserve of Nepal's kings. The resort sits inside it, near the Bagmati and the old temple town of Gokarneshwar, with rooms spread through the grounds in buildings styled with Nepali brick and wood. Spotted deer and monkeys wander between them.

The forest is the main reason to stay: birdsong in the morning, walks under tall trees and a quiet that is hard to find in the city. The resort has an 18-hole golf course laid out through the forest, a spa with an indoor pool, and several restaurants. It is a good base for the eastern sights, with Boudhanath and Pashupatinath about 15 to 20 minutes by car and the airport about 30 minutes.
why: Rooms inside an old forest, with deer and birds in the grounds
Golf, spa and indoor pool for slow days
Close to Boudhanath, Pashupatinath and Gokarneshwar

faqs.q: Where is Gokarna Forest Resort?
faqs.a: It is on the north-eastern edge of Kathmandu, inside the Gokarna forest near Gokarneshwar, about 30 minutes from the airport. Boudhanath and Pashupatinath are roughly 15 to 20 minutes away by car. Thamel is 40 minutes to an hour, depending on traffic.

faqs.q: Does Gokarna Forest Resort have a golf course?
faqs.a: Yes. The resort has an 18-hole golf course laid out through the forest, one of the few in the Kathmandu Valley. Non-guests can sometimes play by arrangement. Check current green fees and availability before you travel. Clubs can usually be hired.

faqs.q: Is Gokarna Forest Resort good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Children usually enjoy seeing deer and monkeys in the grounds, and the forest, gardens and indoor pool give space away from city traffic. It is quieter and greener than central hotels, though you will need a car for sightseeing.

name: Club Himalaya
summary: The first resort hotel on the Nagarkot ridge, opened in 1996 on Windy Hill at about 2,175 m. Rooms open onto balconies facing the Himalaya, and an indoor pool, spa and terrace bar make it a comfortable base for sunrise and ridge walks.
body: Club Himalaya, now operated by ACE Hotels, opened in 1996 and was the first resort on the Nagarkot ridge. It sits on Windy Hill at around 2,175 m, facing north across the valleys to the Himalaya, so most rooms open onto a private balcony where you can watch sunrise without leaving your bed. On clear days the view runs from the Langtang range across Dorje Lakpa to Gaurishankar.

The hotel has an indoor swimming pool, useful on cold mornings, a spa, and a bar with an outdoor terrace and an indoor fireplace for winter evenings. Restaurants serve Nepali, Indian, Chinese and continental food. It is about 1.5 hours from Kathmandu by car, and a good start point for walks along the ridge or down to Changunarayan and Bhaktapur.
why: Balcony rooms facing the Himalaya on Nagarkot's ridge
Indoor pool and fireplace for cold mornings and evenings
Start point for walks to Changunarayan and Bhaktapur

faqs.q: Do all rooms at Club Himalaya have mountain views?
faqs.a: Most rooms open onto a private balcony facing north towards the Himalaya, and that view is the hotel's main appeal. Visibility depends on weather: October to February mornings are clearest. Ask for a mountain-facing room when booking and confirm it on arrival.

faqs.q: How do I get to Club Himalaya Nagarkot?
faqs.a: By car, it takes about 1.5 hours from central Kathmandu via Bhaktapur, climbing the last 20 km through hairpin bends. Most guests use a private car or hotel transfer. Local buses from Bhaktapur reach Nagarkot, but you will need a short walk or taxi to the hotel.

faqs.q: Is it cold at Club Himalaya in winter?
faqs.a: Yes. At around 2,175 m, nights from November to February drop close to freezing and mornings are cold. Rooms are heated, and the indoor pool and fireplace bar help. Bring warm layers, a hat and gloves for sunrise on your balcony.

name: Dwarika's Resort Dhulikhel
summary: A wellness-focused resort from the family behind Dwarika's Hotel, set on terraced hillside outside Dhulikhel with views of the Himalaya. Brick and stone buildings, gardens, yoga and meditation programmes, and a slow pace about 1.5 hours from Kathmandu.
body: Dwarika's Resort Dhulikhel was created by the same family as Dwarika's Hotel in Kathmandu, with a different aim: wellness and quiet. The resort spreads over a terraced hillside above the Araniko Highway, with buildings in brick, stone and wood inspired by Newar and Himalayan design, and gardens that step down the slope. Many rooms and terraces look north to the mountains.

The focus is on slowing down: yoga and meditation sessions, spa treatments, walks, and meals built around fresh, seasonal food. It suits travellers recovering from a trek, or wanting a few calm days before the city. From here, the old town of Dhulikhel, the hike to Namobuddha and the homestays of Panauti are all within easy reach by car or on foot.
why: Hillside setting with Himalayan views from rooms and terraces
Wellness programmes: yoga, meditation and spa
Easy base for Namobuddha, Panauti and Dhulikhel's old town

faqs.q: How far is Dwarika's Resort Dhulikhel from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: About 30 km east, roughly 1.5 hours by car along the Araniko Highway via Bhaktapur and Banepa, depending on traffic and road works. The resort can arrange transfers. It is about 10 minutes from Dhulikhel's old town and 30 minutes from Panauti.

faqs.q: Is Dwarika's Resort Dhulikhel good after a trek?
faqs.a: Yes. Its wellness focus, with yoga, meditation, spa treatments and quiet gardens, makes it a good place to recover after a trek, and its mountain views are a reminder of where you have been. Two or three nights works well.

faqs.q: Can I see the Himalaya from Dwarika's Resort Dhulikhel?
faqs.a: On clear days, yes. The resort faces north across the hills to the Himalaya, with the Langtang range and peaks towards Gaurishankar visible from many terraces and rooms. October to February mornings give the best views; haze and cloud often hide the peaks from March to September.
